name: Law enforcement, corrections and courts

glossary.definition: Agencies with authority share one command post and one set of objectives under a named incident commander. The DOJ review of the Robb Elementary response (Jan 2024) found no one established command.

DOJ recommends five: reasonable belief an abduction occurred; child in imminent danger of serious injury or death; enough descriptive information; child is 17 or younger; child entered in the national crime database with the Child Abduction flag. States set their own (amberalert.ojp.gov).
The facility tally of people in custody by housing area; a discrepancy is reconciled from the movement log.
A court function that must resume, with a recovery time objective (NCSC continuity framing).
At least a primary negotiator, a coach and a team leader who briefs the commander (FBI guidance; agencies vary).

productConventions: Radio traffic and CAD entries use unit names, building-level locations, statuses and 24-hour times.
Command post paperwork uses the ICS forms; one joint statement carries the same numbers for every agency.
Court orders state the court, a fictional case number, the date, the judge and the effective period.
realismRules: Coordination level only: who commands, who is told, what keeps running. Never write entry or breaching methods, weapon handling, tactical positioning, force options, ways to defeat security or detention measures, attack planning, building layouts or security weaknesses.
If the brief asks for tactics, write the coordination decision instead. All people, agencies and case numbers are fictional.
Public messages never name or describe the person responsible. A negotiation log has contact times, decision requests and welfare only: no technique, scripts or dialogue.
Name the incident commander and announce the command post before sending more units; list each agency in unified command.
AMBER: show each criterion as met or not with a reason; the database entry comes before the alert.
Jail counts match the movement log; court systems come back in dependency order (case management before e-filing).

criticalTasks: Name an incident commander and announce the command post before sending more units.
Form unified command with fire, EMS and every agency with authority, and list who is at the command post.
Request mutual aid through the agreed channels and say who leads a multiagency response.
Keep one set of incident objectives for every agency on scene.
Assign radio channels and an interoperability channel so agencies can reach the command post.
Keep a CAD chronology and unit status that every agency can read.
Say what is known and what is not on the radio in unit names, building-level locations and statuses.
Activate a joint information system and release one statement with the same numbers from every agency.
Tell families where to go and when it opens before they crowd the perimeter.
Decide the AMBER Alert criteria with reasons, enter the database record before the alert, and answer tips.
Notify the bar, jurors and the public of court closures in plain language.
Hold the command decisions that law enforcement owns at the command level: who leads, who is told, who is asked for help.
Reconcile a facility count from the movement log and declare it clear on stated facts.
Reconcile conflicting counts and status reports into one picture at the command post.
Track the status of essential court functions against their recovery time objectives.
Open a reunification site or family assistance center and staff it with victim services.
Reunite students and families through an agreed process.
Decide what to shut down and what to leave running when court systems are attacked.
Restore systems in dependency order and confirm each dependency before the next.
